skills.name: Applications of density in engineering and daily life

note.text:
Engineers choose materials partly by density:
• Aircraft and bicycles: aluminium alloys (low density, strong).
• Ships: steel hulls are hollow, so the ship's average density is less than water's and it floats.
• Hot-air balloons rise because hot air is less dense than cold air.
• Life jackets use low-density foam.
• Builders estimate loads: mass = density × volume (concrete ≈ 2400 kg/m³).
• Oil spills float on the sea because oil is less dense than water.

sections.heading: Floating and sinking
sections.text:
An object floats if its average density is less than that of the liquid. A solid steel bar sinks, but a steel ship is mostly air inside, so its average density is less than water's.
Hot air is less dense than cold air, so a hot-air balloon rises. Oil is less dense than water, so an oil spill floats on the sea and can be scooped off.

sections.heading: Choosing materials
sections.text:
• Aircraft, bicycles and car parts: aluminium alloys, strong but light ({2.7} g/cm³ against {7.9} g/cm³ for steel).
• Life jackets and floats: foams of very low density.
• Fishing weights and sinkers: lead, very dense, so a small piece is heavy.
• Boats are built so that they float even when loaded.

sections.heading: Estimating loads
sections.text:
Builders and engineers use m = ρV to know how heavy a structure will be.
A concrete slab {3} m × {2} m × {0.15} m has V = {0.9} m³; at {2400} kg/m³ its mass is {2160} kg.
A {1000} L water tank on a roof adds about {1000} kg: the roof must be designed for that load.

key_words.meaning: total mass ÷ total volume of an object made of several materials
a mixture of metals, such as aluminium alloy
the weight a structure must support

mistake.wrong: A ship floats because steel is light
mistake.right: A ship floats because its average density, with the air inside, is less than water's
mistake.why: Steel is much denser than water. The shape of the hull, full of air, makes the difference.

worked_example.problem: A concrete slab for a house in Bafoussam is {l} m × {w} m × {h} m. Concrete has density {r} kg/m³. Find its mass.
steps: m = ρV = {r} × {roundTo(l * w * h, 0.001)} = {roundTo(r * l * w * h, 1)} kg.

cards.idea: A ship floats because its average density (steel + air inside) is less than water's.
example: A solid steel bar sinks; a hollow steel hull floats.

cards.idea: Low-density materials keep vehicles light: aluminium for aircraft.
Builders use m = ρV to estimate loads.

check.prompt: A concrete pillar has a volume of {V} m³. Concrete has a density of {2400} kg/m³. Find its mass (kg).

pick.q: Why does a large steel ship float when a steel nail sinks?
pick.r: The hollow hull makes the ship's average density less than water's
w: Steel is less dense than water
The ship is lighter than the nail
e: Steel (7.9 g/cm³) is much denser than water.
The ship is far heavier than the nail.
Sea water is slightly denser than fresh water.
pick.y: The air inside the hull lowers the average density.

pick.q: Why does a hot-air balloon rise?
pick.r: Hot air is less dense than the cold air around it
w: The basket is lighter than air
e: Hot air still has mass, just less per cubic metre.
The basket is denser than air; the hot air carries it.
The flame heats the air; it does not push the balloon.
pick.y: Less dense air rises through denser air.

pick.q: After an oil spill, the oil spreads on top of the sea. Why?
pick.r: Oil is less dense than sea water
w: Oil is denser than sea water
e: It floats because of density, even on a calm day.
pick.y: Less dense liquids float on denser ones.

pick.q: Why is aluminium used to make aircraft bodies?
pick.r: It is strong and has a low density
e: A dense metal would make the aircraft too heavy.
Magnetism is not why it is chosen.
A low melting point would be a problem, not an advantage.
pick.y: Strength with low density keeps the aircraft light.

pick.q: Which material is best for a life jacket?
e: Iron is very dense: it sinks.
Lead is very dense: it sinks.
pick.y: A low-density material floats and helps you float.

pick.q: Fishermen in Limbe tie lead weights to their nets. Why lead?
pick.r: Lead is very dense, so a small piece pulls the net down
e: Lead sinks: it is denser than water.
Lead does not dissolve; it is chosen for its density.
pick.y: High density: a small volume has a large mass.

questions.prompt: A concrete pillar has a volume of {V} m³. Concrete has a density of {2400} kg/m³. Find its mass (kg).
A closed hollow tin can has mass {m} g and volume {V} cm³. Find its average density (g/cm³).
solution: Average density = total mass ÷ total volume.
= {m} ÷ {V} = {answer} g/cm³, {m / V < 1 ? 'less than water, so it floats' : 'more than water, so it sinks'}.

questions.prompt: A water tank on a roof holds {L} litres. Water has density {1000} kg/m³. What extra mass does the full tank put on the roof (kg)?

misconceptions.explain: That is the volume in m³. Multiply by the density {1000} kg/m³.
Change litres to m³ first: divide by {1000}.

solution: m = {1000} × {L / 1000} = {answer} kg (each litre of water has a mass of about {1} kg).
